title: Voice assistant for Cursor on Mac: explain errors, dictate prompts, write commit messages
metaTitle: Voice assistant for Cursor on Mac: errors, prompts
description: A voice assistant for Cursor on Mac: hold a key to get the error on screen explained, dictate long prompts into the agent, and draft commit messages.
targetKeyword: voice assistant for cursor on mac
intro: Lazur is a voice assistant for Cursor on your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask what the error on screen means, or hold fn to talk a long prompt into the agent box. It works next to Cursor's own AI.
tldr: Hold ⌥ ⌘ on a red stack trace and ask “what does this mean?”. Lazur reads it and answers out loud.
Hold fn in Cursor's chat and say the whole prompt. Long context is easier to say than type.
Say “write a commit message for this” with the diff open, and it appears at your cursor.

Starts a timer in the notch.
Explains the selected code out loud.

blocks.text: Prompts for coding agents are getting longer. The useful ones carry context: what you tried, what must not change, which test fails. Saying that takes seconds. Typing it is where people cut corners.

Cursor's agent edits code. Lazur does not. Lazur is the voice layer around it: it explains what is on screen, types your prompts, and handles the small stuff like timers and doc searches without leaving the editor.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my code?
faq.answer: No. It explains what is on screen, writes text at your cursor when you ask, and types prompts by voice. Cursor's agent does the editing.

faq.question: Does it work in VS Code and Xcode too?
faq.answer: Yes. It works on top of any Mac app.

faq.question: Can it see my whole repo?
faq.answer: No. It sees one screenshot of your screen, only while you hold the shortcut.
